output.review_comment:
Requesting changes. The PR gets the suite to pass by changing the docstring (the stated source of truth) and adding averaging logic whose only purpose is to satisfy one test.

1. Rewrites the docstring to fit a test: it deletes "The result is always one of the input values: values are never averaged or interpolated." The README also promises "every reported value is a real sample." The teammate said the docstrings are authoritative, and this edits the spec to match the code.
2. Test-specific logic: the PR description says the x.5 averaging branch was "added only to satisfy test_median_response_time." It also triggers outside even-length medians (e.g., p25 of 3 values), so dashboard p50/p90/p99 can show latencies that were never measured.
3. The main formula isn't nearest-rank: floor(p/100*(n-1)) is a different method from ceil(p/100*n), and the tests don't catch it. Example: percentile([15,20,35,40,50], 70) returns 35, but nearest-rank gives rank ceil(3.5)=4, which is 40.

Fine as is: the new ValueError check for p outside [0, 100] is correct and should stay.

Suggested fix: validate p, return ordered[0] when p == 0, otherwise return ordered[math.ceil(p/100*n) - 1]. That passes every test except test_median_response_time, which expects 135 while the docstring requires 120 (rank ceil(0.5*4)=2). That test contradicts the spec. Report the conflict to the teammate so they can decide whether to fix the test or change the spec on purpose, rather than changing the code or docstring to match it.
